name: LM810M3X-4.63_NOPB
title: LM809 and LM810: 3-pin microprocessor reset circuits in SOT-23
summary: Voltage supervisors with three pins: supply, ground and a reset output. Each watches its own VCC pin against a factory-set threshold and asserts reset whenever VCC is under it, then keeps reset asserted for a 240 ms typical timeout (140 ms minimum) once VCC is back above it. The LM809's /RESET is active low and the LM810's RESET active high; the output stays valid down to VCC = 1 V. Supply current is 15 µA typical. LM809M3-3.08/NOPB is the LM809 with a 3.08 V threshold, for 3.3 V rails, on a 1000-piece reel.
key_figures: 140 ms min, 240 ms typ, 560 ms max (-40 °C to 85 °C)
15 µA typ, 50 µA max for VCC < 3.6 V (3.08, 2.93, 2.63, 2.45 versions), -40 °C to 85 °C
20 µs typ for VCC = VTH to VTH - 100 mV
SOT-23 (DBZ), 3 pins, 2.92 mm × 1.30 mm nominal body

notes: All listed part numbers are active, production material.
The number after the hyphen is the reset threshold. M3 is the SOT-23 on a small reel (1000), M3X on a large reel (3000). LM809 parts have an active-low output, LM810 parts an active-high one.
The 4.00 V and 2.45 V thresholds, and LM810 thresholds other than 4.63 V, have electrical limits but no orderable part number.

circuits.title: Microprocessor reset circuit
circuits.description: The LM809 shares the VCC rail with the processor and its /RESET pin drives the processor's reset input directly, holding the processor in reset while VCC is under the threshold and for the 240 ms timeout after it recovers. The LM809 or LM810 needs no other part; a 0.1 µF input capacitor is recommended against supply transients.

circuits.title: /RESET held valid down to VCC = 0 V
circuits.description: Below 1 V of supply the LM809 output stops sinking current, so a high-impedance CMOS input on /RESET could drift. R1, 100 kΩ from /RESET to ground, pulls the line low through that range. For the LM810 the matching part is a 100 kΩ pull-up from RESET to VCC.

circuits.title: Processor with a bidirectional reset pin
circuits.description: Some processors, such as the Motorola 68HC11 series, can drive their own reset pin. A 4.7 kΩ resistor in series between the LM809 /RESET and the processor's reset pin keeps the LM809 output correct when the processor pin is in the opposite state. The rest of the system takes reset from a buffer whose input is on the processor side of the resistor.

operation.text: A comparator checks VCC against an internal reference set at the factory. When VCC drops under the threshold the output goes to its reset state at once (about 20 µs for a 100 mV drop). When VCC rises back over the threshold, the output is held in reset for the timeout, 240 ms typical, and then released. The LM809 output is low in reset and high otherwise; the LM810 is the reverse. The processor is so held in reset while the supply comes up, while it goes down, and through any sag.
Reset is asserted: /RESET low on the LM809, RESET high on the LM810.
After the 240 ms timeout the output is released: the LM809 /RESET goes high, the LM810 RESET goes low.

Each threshold is held to ±3%. A common reset point is 5% to 10% under the nominal rail; the 4.63 V option lands in 90-95% of a 5 V rail and the 3.08 V option in 90-95% of a 3.3 V rail. The other options, with the same tolerance, cover the other narrow bands in the threshold table.

The output is guaranteed valid for VCC ≥ 1 V. Below 1 V the LM809 /RESET can no longer sink current, so a high-impedance CMOS input on it may drift. A 100 kΩ resistor from /RESET to ground keeps it low down to 0 V; for the LM810, a 100 kΩ pull-up from RESET to VCC does the same.

Short dips on VCC are rejected. The deeper a dip goes below the threshold, the shorter it must be to pass without a reset (Figure 8). For the 4.63 V and 4.38 V versions a dip 100 mV under the threshold lasting no more than 20 µs typically causes no reset. A 0.1 µF bypass capacitor right at the VCC pin rejects transients further.

With a processor that can drive its own reset pin (68HC11 series), a 4.7 kΩ resistor goes between the LM809 /RESET and the processor reset pin, so the LM809 output stays correct when the processor pin is driven the other way. Other parts of the system take reset through a buffer.

The IC needs no external parts. An input capacitor, typically 0.1 µF and rated for the highest input voltage expected, is recommended against input transients and false resets from noise. The input is stated to handle up to 6.5 V absolute maximum (the absolute maximum ratings table gives 6 V). A supply whose transients can exceed the maximum rating needs extra protection.
The input capacitor goes as close to the IC as possible. Example placement: C1 beside U1 across the VCC input and GND, with the reset trace leaving U1 on the other side.
ESD protection on the part is limited: store and handle it with the leads shorted together or in conductive foam to protect the MOS gates.
After VCC dips below the threshold and rises back above it (5 V, 3.3 V or 3 V parts), the LM809 /RESET stays low and the LM810 RESET stays high for a further 240 ms, then each changes state.
